GyroMEMS Simulation

How does your phone know that it's rotating even when you can't see the movement ?

MEMS Gyroscope Die [3D Model] Drag to Orbit ⟲
Package: QFN-32 Proof Mass: 1.20 µg

Inside your phone is a tiny sensor called a MEMS Gyroscope (Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems). It detects the speed and direction of rotation, allowing applications to respond to movement.

But how does it do that?

Inside the gyroscope, a tiny structure called a proof mass vibrates continuously back and forth along the X-axis. This is known as the drive motion.

When the phone rotates, the moving mass experiences a force called the Coriolis Force. This force causes the mass to move in a perpendicular direction, along the sensing axis (Z-axis). This additional movement is called the sense motion.

The sensor detects this tiny displacement and converts it into an electrical signal. By processing this signal, the gyroscope determines the phone's angular velocity — how fast and in which direction it is rotating.

This is how a microscopic vibrating structure helps your phone understand movement!

Sense Mode

04 CAPACITIVE SENSING

Capacitive Sensing

Signal Processing

The circuit calculates angular velocity.

06 FINAL OUTPUT

Understanding the Simulation Readings

The table updates in real time to show what happens inside the simulated gyroscope and how its readings are related:

Coriolis Force (nN): Changes as the phone rotates. It depends on the angular velocity, the vibrating mass, and its drive velocity. The greater the angular velocity, the greater the Coriolis force, assuming the other variables remain constant.

Angular Velocity (rad/s): Calculated from the change in the phone's orientation divided by the time taken. A larger angle change in the same time means a higher angular velocity.

Rotation Direction: Determined by the direction and signs of the angular velocity components around the Pitch and Yaw axes.

Orientation Change (°): Calculated by comparing the phone's current orientation with its starting orientation. It represents the accumulated change in position, rather than how fast the phone is rotating.

Sensor Drift (°): Represents the error that can accumulate over time due to sensor bias and noise. A constant bias can cause the estimated orientation to gradually deviate from the actual orientation.

Scientific References

Governing Laws & Equations

I. Coriolis Force on Vibrating Proof Mass
Fc = −2 m (ω × vd)
II. Quaternion Angular Velocity & Direction
ω(t) = (2 / Δt) · Im( q(t) ⊗ q*(t − Δt) )
III. Relative Orientation Change
Δq = q(t) ⊗ q0* ,   Δθ = 2 arccos(|Δqw|)
IV. Gyroscope Bias & Drift Integration
ω̃(t) = ω(t) + b0 + η(t)
V. MEMS Drive-Mode Harmonic Motion
xd(t) = Ad sin(2π fd t)
VI. MEMS Sense-Mode Damped Oscillator
m ÿs + cs ẏs + ks ys = Fc,sense(t)
VII. Oscillation Frequency Measurement
fmeasured = 1 / ΔTperiod
